literature_notes: DPP10 (Q9Y3Q4) is a type II single-pass transmembrane protein: N-terminus residues 1–34 are intracellular, TM spans 35–55, and the large ectodomain runs 56–796. L1 (HA/DPP10), L2 (GFP-DPP10_789), and L3 (mEGFP-DPP10) all report N-terminal fusions; because the N-terminus is intracellular, every one of these tags sits on the cytoplasmic face and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. L4 reports N→Q substitutions at N90, N119, N257, and N342 that reduce plasma-membrane trafficking by >60%; these are glycosylation sites whose integrity is required for surface delivery, not tag-insertion sites, and they are recorded in other_positions as abrogates_function. No ledger line grounds an insertion that is both (a) in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct and (b) placed on the extracellular face. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: HA/DPP10 N-terminal HA fusion confirmed surface-expressed complex by co-IP, but the N-terminus (residues 1–34) is intracellular in this type II TM protein, so the tag faces the cytoplasm.
